Rules / Modernization

SK1005 Use a file-scoped namespace

A file with exactly one block-scoped namespace and nothing beside it can use namespace X;.

CategoryModernization
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floorC# 10.0
Since0.6
SupersedesIDE0161

Why

One level of indentation across every file in the repository, for no expressive gain. The configuration this tool serves already says csharp_style_namespace_declarations = file_scoped; the rule is what makes that true in code an agent wrote rather than only in code the IDE touched.

Example

Instead of:

namespace Vixen.Core {
    public sealed class Archetype;
}

Write:

namespace Vixen.Core;

public sealed class Archetype;

The ReSharper mapping

ReSharper has no inspection id for this: it drives the conversion from csharp_style_namespace_declarations = file_scoped:suggestion and reports the result under resharper_arrange_namespace_body_highlighting = hint. Two mechanisms, two severities, one concept — so this rule maps to no key at all. docs/plan/16 § Q5.

When it does not fire

Only fires when the compilation unit contains exactly one namespace declaration, that namespace is the only member of the unit, it is block-scoped, it contains no nested namespace declaration, and it has no attribute lists or extern aliases after it. A file with two namespaces cannot be converted at all and is not reported; a file whose namespace declaration carries a #if inside its braces is skipped, because the conversion moves a brace the disabled branch may own.

Configuration

  • csharp_style_namespace_declarations
  • dotnet_diagnostic.SK1005.severity
